user.title: Choose where to observe from
user.description: Passes are predicted on your Home Assistant, from CelesTrak's orbital data for about 970 bright satellites. The location defaults to your home. Two things reveal it: the cloud cover forecast sends its coordinates to Open-Meteo (you can switch this off in the options), and the street view loads map tiles of the surrounding area from OpenFreeMap and AWS.

data_description.name: Used as the device name, for example "Home" or "Cabin".
data_description.elevation: In meters above sea level. A rough value is fine.

reconfigure.title: Move this location
reconfigure.description: Correct where passes are predicted for. The location keeps its entities, and the dashboard cards that show it keep working.

data_description.elevation: In meters above sea level. A rough value is fine.

error.invalid_location: Enter a latitude between -90° and 90° and a valid longitude.
error.name_required: Enter a name for this location.
error.invalid_elevation: Enter the elevation as a number of meters.
error.cannot_connect: Could not download the satellite catalog. Check that Home Assistant can reach the internet, then try again.
error.download_limited: CelesTrak, where the orbital data comes from, is not allowing another download yet. Try again in two hours.
error.unknown: Unexpected error while loading the satellite catalog. The log has the details.

abort.already_configured: This location is already set up.

data.show_in_sidebar: Show Satellite Spotter in the sidebar
data.show_in_calendar: Show the passes in the calendar

data_description.brightness_cutoff: A pass is listed only if it gets at least this bright. Magnitudes run backward, so a lower number means brighter: 2.25 suits a suburban sky, 1 leaves the easy ones, and below 0 only the dazzling ones.
data_description.cloud_forecast: Shows how cloudy it is expected to be at each pass. Unless you choose a weather entity below, Open-Meteo receives this location's coordinates, rounded to about a kilometer, every hour.
data_description.weather_entity: Optional. Takes the clouds from this entity's hourly forecast, and Open-Meteo is not asked. Without cloud coverage in that forecast, passes show no clouds.
data_description.alert_lead_minutes: The "Visible pass soon" and "Bright pass soon" sensors turn on this long before the brightest satellite of the pass appears.
data_description.min_elevation: A satellite counts only while it is at least this high. Raise it if trees or buildings hide your horizon.
data_description.follow_entity: Optional, for travel. Passes are worked out for wherever this person or tracker is, once more than 25 km away, and at most every half hour. Open-Meteo then learns roughly where they are, unless you use a weather entity, and everyone who can open the page can see it.
data_description.show_in_sidebar: Adds a Satellite Spotter page to the sidebar with the passes, a 3D globe and a street-level view of the sky. The street view loads map tiles of the area around the location from OpenFreeMap and AWS (and from Esri with aerial imagery). The dashboard cards work either way.
data_description.show_in_calendar: Adds a calendar of the passes of the next five days, each with when and where to look. Calendar triggers can then start automations before a pass.
data_description.units: For distances and speeds on the globe and in the street view. "Automatic" follows Home Assistant's unit system.

street_view.name: Street view photos
street_view.description: The street view shows your street in a 360° photo taken near home, or the 3D model where there is none. Panoramax needs no key. Mapillary needs a free access token and Google Street View a Google Cloud API key: with them, those services' photos are offered too. Browsers fetch the photos themselves, so administrators' browsers receive the keys; other users get Panoramax's photos only.

data_description.street_source: "Best available" takes the best photo near home from every service there is a key for. A single service shows only its photos, and the 3D model none. Each browser can still switch in the street view's Layers menu.
data_description.mapillary_token: Free: on mapillary.com, under Developers, register an application and copy its client token (MLY|…). Mapillary receives the area around home when the street view looks for photos.
data_description.google_api_key: A key of a Google Cloud project with billing on and the Map Tiles API enabled. Restrict it to the Map Tiles API and to your Home Assistant's address. Google's free tier covers about 100,000 tiles a month, and a photo takes about 40 to 140 of them.

error.invalid_number: Enter a number within the range shown.
error.google_key_needed: Enter a Google Cloud API key to show Google Street View photos.
error.mapillary_token_needed: Enter a Mapillary access token to show Mapillary photos.
error.mapillary_token_format: A Mapillary access token looks like MLY|1234…|abcd…: copy the client token of your application on mapillary.com.

catalog_stale.message: The satellite catalog's orbital elements are {age} days old and could not be refreshed ({error}); predictions are paused until a fresh catalog downloads

catalog_stale_upstream.message: The satellite catalog's orbital elements are {age} days old, and CelesTrak's own data is just as old; predictions are paused until a fresh catalog downloads

unknown_location.message: This Satellite Spotter location does not exist.

location_not_loaded.message: This Satellite Spotter location is not ready yet.

catalog_stale.title: Satellite predictions are paused
catalog_stale.description: The orbital elements in the satellite catalog are {age} days old (the median over all satellites), and no fresher catalog could be downloaded ({error}). Predictions from elements this old would be misleading, so the Satellite Spotter entities are unavailable until a download succeeds. Check that Home Assistant can reach the internet: the orbital data comes from CelesTrak. This message goes away by itself once a fresh catalog arrives.

get_passes.name: Get passes
get_passes.description: Lists a location's predicted passes, soonest first, with optional filters.

config_entry_id.name: Location
config_entry_id.description: The location to list passes for.

pass_id.name: Pass
pass_id.description: Only this pass, by its id: a calendar event's uid or a sensor's pass_id.

start.name: From
start.description: Only passes still going after this moment. By default, those not yet over.

end.name: Until
end.description: Only passes starting before this moment.

min_rating.name: Minimum rating
min_rating.description: Only passes rated at least this.

max_cloud_cover.name: Maximum cloud cover
max_cloud_cover.description: Leave out passes forecast to be cloudier than this. Passes without a forecast are kept.

bright_only.name: Bright passes only
bright_only.description: Only passes that count as bright.

kinds.name: Kinds of satellite
kinds.description: Only passes that include one of these.

satellite.name: Satellite name
satellite.description: Only passes with a satellite whose name contains this.
